analysis: Reviewed docs/developer/build.md (head lines 892-1170, which show only unchanged surrounding content; the changed hunk is in lines 622-633 and 666-679, shown only as a patch excerpt) and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (patch plus base text). Changes are CI-routing metadata: the test now pins PRODUCTION_SIZES={8x16,12x32} in place of VALID_SIZES, and PLAN_LANES sizes are bumped from 4x16/4x24 to 8x16, with test-cluster-gpu-2 at 12x32. The docs record that the sandbox plane does not sign 4x16/4x24 and that the sizes are interim. None of this touches the provider runtime, the WebSocket contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058), key custody, or inference data paths. It also adds no credentials, no permissions changes, no new network endpoints and no new release-path routing. The test still asserts that unrouted/release workflows keep literal runners (UNROUTED list unchanged), that fork PRs never contact the plane, and that only exact label arrays are accepted, so the runner-selection trust boundary is not weakened. The unit for the second file (56b32aac6a5bee39:0) is metadata only, with no mode change (100755 both sides). Remaining unverified contract: the matching provider-plan.yml change is outside the supplied evidence, and the test's assertions against it (lane sizes in PRODUCTION_SIZES) depend on it staying consistent. That is a CI-consistency question, not a security regression. No findings; no threat-model update needed.
